sections.html:
Colorado's capital sits in the South Platte valley on the plains side of the Front Range. Census takers found 715,522 people in 2020, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 740,613. Denver is also a county, merged since 1902, which means a single government handles assessing, taxing and recording. A seller usually needs fewer phone calls than elsewhere in Colorado.

Renters outnumber owners. Only 48.8% of homes are owner-occupied across 335,428 households (2020 to 2024). The median owner-occupied value is $616,000 and median gross rent is $1,831. A good share of sales involve a landlord, an heir or an investor who wants out. The median covers the entire city. A particular house can price well away from it, depending on condition, neighborhood and lot.

For Denver roofs, hail is the weather problem that costs the most. Among American cities with 50,000 or more people, Denver ranks 10th for hail proneness, and three of the ten costliest hailstorms on record in the country struck here. Snowfall averages 53.5 inches a year, July highs average 89.9 degrees, and the record of 105 degrees was set June 28, 2018.

A beaten-up roof, split siding or a claim that never led to repairs can stall a mortgage-financed sale, because the lender and the inspector both study roofs. Be ready for these questions:

  • Did anyone file a claim for the hail damage, and was the work done, or was it left?
  • How old is the roof, and will a new owner's insurer cover it?
  • Have sun and freeze-thaw cycles marked the stucco, deck or paint?

Paperwork helps. Someone paying cash may also accept the damage as part of the deal.

Taxes in Denver come due after the year they cover, and the Treasury Division collects them.

Payment optionDue date
First installmentLast day of February
Second installmentJune 15
Single full paymentApril 30

Weekend and holiday deadlines roll to the next business day. Statements live online. Look up your address in the property search tool, open Tax Documents and download the year you need. Paying by credit or debit card adds a 2.5% service fee, and an electronic check carries none. You can reach Treasury at 720-913-9300.

On closing day the current year's tax gets divided by the closing agent, one share for you and one for the buyer. Treasury also issues a Certificate of Taxes Due for Real Property, which the title company uses to learn what a parcel owes. Any earlier year still open must be paid for the transfer to be clean. On appeals and assessment timing, the Denver Treasury property tax page is the place to start.

sections.h2: The state fee on a Denver deed
sections.html: When a deed transfers property for more than $500, Colorado adds a documentary fee of $0.01 per $100, as county recording pages explain. Denver files deeds through the same county system. Look for that fee, the recording charge and any transfer forms on your settlement statement. Choosing a cash buyer leaves these items alone, but it can shorten the wait between signing and recording because no lender has to release loan funds.

In Denver, a short-term rental needs a license and has to be the host's own primary residence. The business license number goes in each ad, and violators risk fines or losing the license.

That bites if you own a second Denver property that was running as an Airbnb. With the primary-residence rule, a house its owner does not live in cannot lawfully operate as a short-term rental. Such a house may have to be sold or leased long term, and a buyer who was counting on nightly income may offer less. Read the city's rental, zoning and licensing pages for your address before you list or take an offer.

Jobs in government, hospitals, schools and aviation keep demand strong near downtown. They offer no protection against a layoff, a divorce or an inherited house nobody wants to run. Events like those, more than the market, push Denver owners toward quick sales.

Inherited a house? Collect the documents showing who has authority to sign, and ask the title company what it needs before it books a closing. Own a rental with a tenant in place? Learn early whether a buyer will take it occupied. Cash buyers often do.

Before spending a dollar, price out the one repair a buyer will notice from the street. In Denver that is usually the roof. If a claim was paid and the work never done, expect a buyer's insurer to ask about it, and expect the number on any offer to reflect that. If the claim was settled and the roof replaced, keep the receipts and permit records in one folder.

Cosmetic work rarely pays back on a house that is being sold quickly. Clean it out, mow, and let the buyer decide what they would change. The goal is a clear picture of what the house needs, so the offers you receive are comparable.

Pull four items together: the latest tax statement from the property search tool, any loan payoff details, your lease and rent roll if a tenant lives there, and any city rental license if the house ran as a short-term rental. Having them ready means the title company can start its search the same day you accept an offer, and nobody has to wait on a missing page.

sections.h2: Three ways to sell a Denver house
sections.html:
Owners usually pick between an agent listing, a sale on their own and a cash purchase, and each swaps price for time and effort.

  • Agent listing: often the best price for a house in good shape, though you wait through showings, repair requests after the inspection and the buyer's loan approval.
  • Sale on your own: the commission stays in your pocket, and the pricing, disclosures and forms become your job.
  • Cash sale: the buyer accepts the house in its current state, which means no repair list and, often, a closing day of your choosing.

Cash fits deferred maintenance, hail damage, a tenant in place or an estate that must be settled. A listing fits a clean house and a roomy calendar. Compare both before you decide. Our cash offer comes with no obligation.

sections.h2: Steps in a Denver cash sale
sections.html:
1. Send the address and describe the house.
  2. We review it and return a written offer.
  3. After you accept, a title company searches the record, requests the Certificate of Taxes Due from Treasury and drafts the deed.
  4. You sign, the deed is recorded and the money is yours.

Set the offer beside a listing first if you like. Saying no costs nothing. Keep your tax statement close, since the property search tool lets you download it in a few minutes.

faqs.q: How much is the median home worth in Denver?
faqs.a: Census data for 2020 to 2024 puts the middle of the owner-occupied market at $616,000. Any single house can sit far from that figure, so read it as a citywide benchmark.

faqs.q: When are Denver property taxes due?
faqs.a: You can pay half by the last day of February and half by June 15, or pay everything by April 30. Weekend and holiday deadlines roll forward a business day.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Denver house that was used as a short-term rental?
faqs.a: Yes. Denver requires both a license and a host who lives there, so a house missing either may draw questions from a buyer. A cash buyer can take it as it stands, but settle any city fines or unpaid taxes.

faqs.q: Does hail damage stop me from selling a house in Denver?
faqs.a: No. Hail is so common here that buyers expect it. A damaged roof can pull the price down or complicate financing, so plenty of owners with roof damage look at an as-is sale.

faqs.q: What is the state documentary fee in Colorado?
faqs.a: One cent for every $100 of consideration on a deed above $500. County recording pages describe it that way, and you will see it listed at closing.
